chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: “I do not act upon the statement of a fortune-teller, nor a tracker, nor a thief, and I do not accept the testimony of the transgressor except against himself.”

key_terms.الْفَاسِقِ: an openly sinful or morally corrupt person
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: testimony given in a legal or judicial setting
key_terms.عَرَّافٍ: a fortune-teller; one who claims knowledge of hidden matters
key_terms.عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: against his own self; as a self-incriminating admission
key_terms.قَائِفٍ: a tracker or one who makes judgments by traces or resemblance

ai.seo_question: Whose testimony and statements are rejected in Islamic legal judgment according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a judicial principle attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding unreliable testimony and statements. It rejects reliance on the word of discredited or morally compromised persons, while allowing a fāsiq’s admission only against his own self.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3306 - And it was narrated by Muhammad bin Qais from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him,
used to say: "I do not act upon the statement of a fortune-teller, nor a tracker, nor a thief, and I do not accept the testimony of a transgressor except against himself."
